question.text: Three members of the House of Medici went on to hold this office in Rome, taking the names Leo X, Clement VII, and Leo XI.
question.answerHtml: Pope [or “the papacy;” or Supreme Pontiff; or Pontifex Maximus; or Bishop of Rome]
question.clue: Julius II was labeled the "warrior" one of these people after he formed the Holy League.

swap.text: This pope, who served during World War II, has been called "Hitler's Pope" for not doing enough to stop the Holocaust.
swap.clue: While on trial, Karl Wolff testified that he had been ordered to kidnap this leader, who gave a "Christmas Broadcast" in support of one group who had "been consigned to death or to a slow decline".

question.leadin: This term sometimes refers to the period of antipopes during the Avignon Papacy.
question.text: Name this term which also applies to an exile of Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: This period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.

swap.leadin: Due to their military-like structure, members of this group are sometimes called "God's Marines."
swap.text: Name this Catholic religious order founded by Ignatius Loyola. Members of this group included Francis Xavier, who traveled to Japan as a missionary.
swap.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the investiture controversy.
question.text: The controversy over appointing bishops was sparked by the reforms launched by the seventh pope of this name. The thirteenth pope of this name created the modern calendar.
question.clue: Henry IV walked to Canossa in a hair shirt to have an excommunication that was given to him by a pope of this name rescinded during the Investiture Controversy.

swap.leadin: Debate persists whether the slogan "God wills it" is appropriately attributed to this pope.
swap.text: Name this pope credited with inciting the First Crusade at the conclusion of the Council of Clermont in 1095.
swap.answerHtml: Pope Urban II [prompt on "Odo de Lagery"; or "Otto de Lagery"; or "Otho de Lagery"; or "Eudes de Lagery"]
swap.clue: This pope allied himself with Roger I of Sicily, and he was heavily influenced by a delegation sent by Alexius I Komnenos.

question.leadin: Terrorists planned to assassinate this pope during a visit to the Philippines in the first phase of the Bojinka Plot.
question.text: Name this pope who established World Youth Day in 1985. This pope's visit to his home country motivated the formation of the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule in that country.
question.clue: This man officially condemned Liberation Theology, and he unofficially supported the Solidarity movement in his home country.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of Malta.
swap.text: This Christian military order ruled Malta for over two and a half centuries, until Ferdinand von Hompesch zu Bolheim surrendered it to Napoleon in 1798.
swap.answerHtml: Knights Hospitaller [or Knights of Saint John, accept Order in place of “Knights” in either]
swap.clue: This group, founded by the Blessed Gerard, controlled the fortresses of Margat (mar-GAH) and Krak des Chevaliers ("crack" deh sheh-val-YAY) before it was forced from the Holy Land.

question.leadin: It also dealt with the Clunian reforms of the Church.
question.text: Name this 1095 council that, more notably, called the First Crusade.
question.clue: Due to an adulterous relationship with Bertrade de Montfort, Countess of Anjou, Philip I was excommunicated at this church council, which was preceded by the council of Placentia.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the First Crusade for the stated points.
swap.text: For 10 points, this pope's Sermon of Clermont called for the crusade.
swap.answerHtml: Urban II [prompt on Urban; or Odo of Lagery] [10/15/20] 10 for one, 15 for two, and 20 for all three, name the three principalities established under the Kingdom of Jerusalem by the First Crusade. ANSWER: Antioch, Edessa, Tripoli
swap.clue: This leader wrote a letter of instruction to the Flemish mentioning Adhemar of Le Puy, as reported on by Baldric of Dol and Robert the Monk.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a church council.
question.text: Called for the purpose of ending the Great Schism, this 1414 council compelled all three competing popes to withdraw and elected Martin V.

swap.leadin: It resulted in troops led by Guillaume de Nogaret storming the papal residence at Anagni and holding Boniface VIII captive for three days.
swap.text: Name this papal bull issued by Boniface that proclaimed the supremacy of the church over temporal powers.
swap.clue: This declaration was preceded by the bull Etsi de statu, which reversed a previous bull issued only a year and a half prior regarding taxing the clergy.

question.leadin: This pope praised "African values" such as "community life" in his "Message to Africa," which contained a thinly veiled appeal to aid the Catholics of Igboland in the Biafran War.
question.text: Name this pope who canonized the Uganda martyrs and later visited Kampala in 1969 in the first papal trip to Africa. This pope presided over the end of Vatican II after the death of John XXIII ("the twenty-third").
question.answerHtml: Paul VI [or Paulus VI or Paolo VI; or Giovanni Battista Enrico Antonio Maria Montini; prompt on Paul or Paulus or Paolo]
question.clue: In July, this pope issued the encyclical Humanae vitae, which condemned artificial birth control. In 1968, this pope who closed the Second Vatican Council also beatified the Korean Martyrs.

swap.text: Clement VII was the first of two of these popes, who are not considered official by the Roman Catholic Church. Modern groups of them include the Sedevacantist ones and the Conclavist ones.
swap.clue: This term used to describe individuals who oppose the elected bishop of Rome and consequently makes a widely accepted claim to the papal throne.

question.leadin: Answer the following about French popes.
question.text: No Frenchman has been elected pope since Gregory XI ("the eleventh"), the last of a line of seven French popes who presided from this city. Clement V moved the seat of the papacy to this city from Rome, where it remained during the "Babylonian captivity."
question.clue: Six elections were held in this city's Palais des Papes during a period alternately called the "Babylonian Captivity."

swap.text: The Swiss Confederation was notably invited by Holy Roman Emperor Sigismund to sit at this 15th-century ecumenical council, which issued the Sacrosancta but mostly failed in its reform attempts.
swap.clue: It was here that Pope Gregory XII helped elect Oddone Colonna as his own replacement.

question.text: This unrecognized 1409 council attempted to sort out the Western Schism by deposing both Benedict and Gregory, but fucked up by electing the compromise pope Alexander V.
question.clue: Philargi was elected and took the name Alexander V, but the results were ignored since Urban VI and Clement VII both refused to recognize this council.

swap.text: The militia that seized Apatzingan did so in opposition to this cartel, which issued a moratorium on violence during a visit by Benedict XVI. It is most active in the Michoacan state, where it extorts money from avocado farmers.
swap.clue: This group's members were exempted from paying taxes by Pope Innocent II and acted as bankers for travelers to Jerusalem.

question.text: In 1644, this pope born Maffeo Barberini died. He was a friend of Galileo and it was he to whom Galileo retorted, "But it does move."
question.clue: Unlike his successor Innocent X, this pope followed a relatively pro-French policy which was concerned with maintaining neutrality during the Thirty Years' War.

swap.text: Between his rise and getting his head used as a soccer ball, Mussolini negotiated the Lateran Treaty with this polity that was then headed by Pius XI.
swap.answerHtml: Vatican City [accept Holy See; prompt on Catholic Church or equivalents]
swap.clue: A meeting in this city declared that doctrines issued ex cathedra are infallible, and was prompted by the Syllabus of Errors of Pius IX.
